messages:
alex: FYA: today we had a client report where hedged upstreams produced interleaved frames, client saw garbled stream. attaching quick trace and notes.

priya: Which protocol and any clues about framing?

alex: grpc over h2, bidirectional. The gateway hedged at ~200ms and merged responses from two upstreams. Trace excerpt: 

alex: ```
EGRESS: req=xyz789 hedge_id=7 -> up-a (primary)
INGRESS: frame(seq=0,len=640,partial=true,origin=up-a)
INGRESS: frame(seq=3,len=128,partial=true,origin=up-b)
INGRESS: frame(seq=1,len=512,partial=false,origin=up-a)
// client observed seq 0,3,1 -> client reassemble failed
```

joel: Hmm. Sequence numbers were per-upstream so merging broke ordering. We need a gateway-side sequencing envelope.

morgan: Agreed. Proposal: gateway assigns per-request stream_epoch + frag_index and emits X-RW-Stream-Epoch / X-RW-Frag-Idx headers on egress. Ingress resequencer uses (epoch, idx) to reorder.

priya: Why epoch + idx vs single monotonic seq? Epoch lets us invalidate earlier hedges when primary switches. If primary changes, bump epoch so late fragments from old primary are ignored.

joel: Details: envelope fields: epoch(u32), frag_idx(u32), final_bit(bool), origin_hint(string). Resequencer maintains next_idx per epoch. If epoch changes, flush/abort previous window.

alex: Need bounded memory. Suggest per-request slot limit (default 64 frags) and per-route shared budget. If exceeded, either drop older fragments or apply backpressure to upstreams (send RST/abort for hedges).

priya: Eviction policies: drop-oldest, drop-largest, or refuse new hedged connections. I prefer refusing additional hedges once budget exhausted to avoid silent data loss. Also emit metric stream.reseq_drops and stream.reseq_budget_exhausted.

morgan: Important: signature/signed-headers interaction. Many clients sign headers; adding X-RW-* might break end-to-end signatures. Options: 1) gateway-only headers removed before upstreams that validate signatures; 2) sign them inside gateway credentials; 3) make resequencing opt-in for routes that don't require client-signed headers.

joel: We should avoid changing client-visible signed headers. Make gateway strip the env-headers before reaching upstreams that check signatures. For transparency, also include a trailer checksum header signed by gateway so clients can verify final integrity.

priya: For gRPC streaming we also need to respect flow-control. Resequencer should not buffer unlimited data even if frag count is low. Use a slot budget measured in bytes and fragments. Expose per-request bytes_buffered gauge.

alex: Failure modes: a malicious upstream could replay old frags with a newer epoch. We should include an origin_id and maybe a short MAC keyed by gateway per-backend to prevent cross-upstream spoofing. But that increases crypto. Maybe accept origin_id + TLS channel-binding for now.

morgan: Perf concerns: adding headers + small ring buffer + mem allocs. We'll microbench in proxy-v2, measure p50/p95/p99 for small and long streams under hedged fanout. Establish safe defaults: 64 frags, 256KB per request.

joel: Rollout plan: 1) implement resequencer behind feature flag + route opt-in, 2) unit tests + chaos sim (dual upstreams, delayed fragments), 3) perf harness, 4) canary in low-traffic region, 5) broader rollout.

priya: Also add admin controls: per-tenant knobs, global emergency-disable flag, and dashboards (slots, bytes, drops, hedged_conflicts).

alex: I'll file a task and start a POC.

infra-bot: created ticket RINF-4367 for resequencer POC + perf harness <https://phabricator/internal/RINF-4367>

morgan: I'll join POC pairing for the harness. Priya can take metrics/dashboards. Joel can review API/envelope spec. Alex take lead on POC impl.

alex: Thanks team, drafting short RFC and will link to RINF-4367. :thumbsup:
